title: tenant-imposter-token-and-audit-drop-during-kms-rotation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Production customers on Private deployments reported that after scheduled KMS envelope rotation events, some service-issued tokens briefly gained the ability to impersonate tenant-scoped identities outside their expected tenant boundary while corresponding audit events for those requests were not recorded. Root cause spans three interacting faults: (1) race between KMS envelope unwrap and identity claim normalization that allowed stale service tokens to be accepted for a short window, (2) control-plane behavior that silently dropped audit batch flushes during KMS rotation, and (3) a legacy tenant-lookup fallback that interpreted an empty tenant claim as 'system' when KMS unwrap returned unexpected metadata. This ticket drives the urgent patch to eliminate the window and reinstate reliable audit emission during rotations.
impact_summary: Multiple enterprise Private customers observed cross-tenant impersonation attempts and missing audit records for 90s windows around rotation events. No confirmed data exfiltration; however regulatory audit trails were incomplete for impacted time ranges. Severity: P0 operational security for Private customers.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy private control-plane vX with KMS envelope rotation scheduled every 30m in a multi-tenant cluster.
2) Issue service token bound to tenant A with close-to-expiry KMS envelope.
3) Trigger a KMS rotation while concurrently submitting an API call that relies on control-plane tenant-lookup fallback.
4) Observe that the token is accepted for a request that targets tenant B and that audit events for that request are absent from the audit store for ~60-120s.
5) Reproduce by fast-forwarding rotation in staging to confirm race conditions and missing flushes.
temporary_mitigations: 1) Disable legacy tenant-lookup fallback via feature-flag on affected clusters (hotfix applied by SRE).
2) Enforce synchronous KMS unwrap acknowledgement in the control-plane ingress path for Private clusters (config toggle), preventing acceptance of tokens until unwrap completes.
3) Instruct support to throttle scheduled rotations for impacted customers and extend rotation window with manual coordination until patch rolls out.
root_cause_analysis: Race between KMS unwrap callback and tenant-claim normalization path allowed acceptance of a token before tenant claim verification completed.
Audit emitter batches were paused during rotation cleanup and a path existed that dropped the in-memory batch commit when unwrap returned special metadata.
Fallback path interpreted missing tenant claim as a privileged system tenant for backward compatibility; combined with (1) this produced cross-tenant acceptance.
patch_description: A1: Harden identity parsing to require explicit tenant claim; reject tokens with missing tenant claim rather than falling back.
A2: Make KMS unwrap idempotent and return a deterministic status to the control-plane; accept requests only after unwrap success or explicit failure (no implicit accept).
A3: Audit emitter changes: ensure rotation hooks flush and persist in-progress batches before envelope rotation completes; add ack and retry logic for audit writes during rotation.
A4: Add unit + integration tests that simulate concurrent rotation + request flows and assert no cross-tenant acceptance and guaranteed audit persistence.

test_plan: Unit tests for identity parser covering missing/empty/invalid tenant claims.
Integration test harness that drives concurrent KMS rotations and high QPS request streams from multiple tenants.
End-to-end verification in a Private staging cluster with canary traffic that validates no audit gaps and strict tenant isolation under rotation stress tests.
Post-deploy synthetic monitor that runs tenant-isolation checks every 30s for 24h after rollout.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PRs to control-plane and audit-service trunk after security review and 1 approver from Security team.
2) Canary deploy to subset of Private clusters (5% of clusters, low-risk customers) and run smoke tests for 2 hours.
3) If canary is green, ramp to 50% over 1 hour with continuous audit validation.
4) Full rollout across remaining Private clusters with 10-minute health checks and ability to pause between batches.
5) Notify customers and support with release notes and rotation coordination guidance.
rollback_plan: If canary shows regression: immediate rollback of control-plane binary to previous version and re-enable fallback tenant-lookup flag; revert audit-service change if necessary.
Post-rollback action: collect debug logs and extend SRE mitigation window until fix is reworked.
acceptance_criteria: No cross-tenant request acceptance observed in canary for 48h under rotation stress.
Audit service persists all audit events during and after rotation with no missing sequence gaps for test windows.
Security review sign-off and automated tests added to CI preventing regressions.
